summary: This resolution directs the President to remove US Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon within 7 days of adoption, while allowing security cooperation with Lebanese forces and protection of diplomatic facilities.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the removal of U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon but contains no provisions, authorizations, or restrictions related to federal spending levels, appropriations, or budget authority. Any spending effects would be indirect and secondary at best.
The resolution addresses military withdrawal under the War Powers Resolution and has no connection to tax policy, rates, or revenue measures.
No provisions in the bill relate to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The bill concerns U.S. military forces abroad and has zero bearing on domestic gun regulations or rights.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions appear in the text.
The concurrent resolution is silent on reproductive health or abortion access.

Section 1 explicitly directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon within 7 days. This directly reduces U.S. military engagement and associated defense activities in the region, producing a moderate negative effect on the scale of military operations even though dollar amounts are not specified.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related content exists in the bill.
The measure does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No education policy, funding, or school-choice provisions are present.
The bill contains nothing related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No criminal sentencing, policing, or justice-system reforms are addressed.
The resolution does not touch on tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
While reduced military operations could produce minor budgetary savings, the bill itself makes no reference to deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal policy.
No provisions concern LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
Section 2 permits continued security cooperation with the Lebanese Armed Forces but does not authorize, expand, or cut foreign aid programs.
The bill has no relation to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions are included.
The concurrent resolution does not address labor rights, unions, or employment policy.
No content relates to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
